summary:
Paris is the capital and largest city of France, located on the Seine in the centre of the Île-de-France region [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]].

Its population within the city proper (the commune of Paris) is roughly 2.1 million: the official INSEE legal municipal population for the 2023 reference year is 2,103,778, in force as of 1 January 2026 [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]], and recent estimates show a slow decline to about 2.05–2.09 million [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]] [[web_65e4e5164565458316c7430b]].

Broader definitions are substantially larger: the Paris metropolitan area (aire urbaine) has about 15.1 million inhabitants [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]], the Île-de-France region about 12.5 million [[web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162]], and the Métropole du Grand Paris about 6.9 million [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]].

The "roughly 2.1 million" figure refers to the city proper; the wider region is on the order of 12–15 million depending on the definition used [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]] [[web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162]] [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]].

sections.title: The capital of France
sections.markdown:
Paris is the capital and largest city of France, with an estimated city population of about 2.04 million in an area of 105.4 km² as of January 2026 [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]]. It is located on the river Seine in the centre of the Île-de-France region and is the largest metropolitan area in the European Union [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]]. Administratively, Paris is both a commune and a department (INSEE code 75056), divided into twenty arrondissements [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]].

As the capital, Paris is the seat of France's national government: the President resides at the Élysée Palace, the Prime Minister at the Hôtel Matignon, and both houses of the French Parliament sit on the Rive Gauche — the Senate in the Palais du Luxembourg and the National Assembly in the Palais Bourbon [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]]. The city also hosts the headquarters of several international organisations, including UNESCO and the OECD [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]]. The capital status is not in dispute across any of the sources; the substantive question is the population figure, which varies by definition and reference date.

sections.title: Population of the city proper
sections.markdown:
The authoritative figure for the city proper comes from INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques), France's national statistics institute. For the 2023 reference year, INSEE records a municipal population of 2,103,778 for the commune of Paris, a "counted separately" population of 15,634, and a total population of 2,119,412 [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]]. These reference populations entered into force on 1 January 2026 and were authenticated by decree n° 2025-1362 of 26 December 2025 [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]]. The municipal population is the figure used for statistical purposes; the total population is more often used for legislative or regulatory applications [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]].

Independent sources reproduce the same 2023 figure. Citypopulation.de, which cites INSEE as its source, lists 2,103,778 for the commune of Paris as of 1 January 2023 [[web_4b9a68f2101be4b45f3c9513]] [[web_955d914bb5822b60e6f8869b]]. INSEE's own dossier complet for the commune confirms 2,103,778 for 2023, alongside 2,187,526 for 2017 and 2,240,621 for 2012 [[web_01dcf2219a78d49da073bba6]] [[web_509ca9307b054327c0afd19e]].

More recent estimates show a continuing decline. INSEE's Flash publication of October 2024 reports 2,087,600 people living in Paris in 2024, 45,500 fewer than three years earlier [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]]. The Wikipedia infobox and the EU city list both give 2,047,602 for 1 January 2026 [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]] [[web_65e4e5164565458316c7430b]], and the European cities list gives 2,048,472 for 1 January 2025 [[web_8785c58202edd0de44471720]]. One Wikipedia passage gives 2,102,650 for January 2023 [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]], a figure slightly below the INSEE legal population of 2,103,778 for the same reference year — a small discrepancy likely reflecting different estimation methods (annual estimates versus the census-based legal population), but immaterial to the "roughly 2.1 million" answer.

The figures are summarised below, drawing on INSEE's legal population [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]], INSEE's Flash estimate [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]], the Wikipedia infobox and EU city list [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]] [[web_65e4e5164565458316c7430b]], the European cities list [[web_8785c58202edd0de44471720]], and citypopulation.de [[web_4b9a68f2101be4b45f3c9513]]:

| Source | Population | Reference date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| INSEE legal municipal population | 2,103,778 | 2023 reference year, in force 1 Jan 2026 [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]] |
| INSEE total population (municipal + counted separately) | 2,119,412 | 2023 reference year [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]] |
| INSEE Flash estimate | 2,087,600 | 2024 [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]] |
| Wikipedia infobox / EU city list | 2,047,602 | 1 Jan 2026 [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]] [[web_65e4e5164565458316c7430b]] |
| European cities list | 2,048,472 | 1 Jan 2025 [[web_8785c58202edd0de44471720]] |
| Citypopulation.de | 2,103,778 | 1 Jan 2023 [[web_4b9a68f2101be4b45f3c9513]] |

All of these fall within "roughly 2.1 million" for the city proper [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]] [[web_4b9a68f2101be4b45f3c9513]] [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]] [[web_65e4e5164565458316c7430b]]. The differences among them reflect the documented ongoing population decline rather than any contradiction among sources: INSEE reports that Paris has been losing residents for decades, with the decline driven by a negative migration balance that the natural surplus does not offset [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]], and the city's population fell by 122,919, about five percent, between 2013 and 2023 [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]].

sections.title: Broader definitions: metropolitan area and region
sections.markdown:
The population figure depends heavily on which boundary is used, and the sources are explicit that the city proper is much smaller than the urbanised area around it. The Paris metropolitan area (aire urbaine, as of the 2020 revision) covers 1,929 communes and 18,941 km², with a population of 15,064,617 [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]]. This statistical area describes the reach of commuter movement to and from Paris and extends beyond the administrative Île-de-France region into nine surrounding departments [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]]. Paris itself, at 2,165,423, is the largest city within it [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]].

Two other definitions are commonly cited. The Métropole du Grand Paris, an administrative structure for cooperation between Paris and its nearest suburbs created in January 2016, covers 814 km² and had a population of 6.945 million in 2015 [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]]. The Île-de-France region, the administrative region containing Paris, had a population of 12,463,067 as of January 2023, or 18.3 percent of the population of France [[web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162]]. INSEE's Flash publication notes that Paris accounts for 17 percent of the Île-de-France population on less than 1 percent of the regional territory [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]].

These are not conflicting figures but different scopes: the city proper (~2.1 million) [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]], the Grand Paris cooperation structure (~6.9 million) [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]], the region (~12.5 million) [[web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162]], and the broader commuter-based metropolitan area (~15.1 million) [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]]. A reader asking for "the population of Paris" should be aware that the answer ranges from about 2.1 million to about 15 million depending on the boundary chosen [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]] [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]]; the city proper is the standard referent for "the capital" [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]].

sections.title: Population trend and density
sections.markdown:
Paris's population has been declining for decades, which explains the small differences among the figures cited above. The city reached a historic high of 2.9 million in 1921, then declined at every census between 1954 and 1999, falling to 2,125,246 in 1999 [[web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162]]. INSEE's official series shows 2,590,771 in 1968 falling to 2,103,778 in 2023, with a mid-2000s rebound to 2,240,621 in 2012 [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]] [[web_01dcf2219a78d49da073bba6]]. The decline resumed after 2012: the average annual change was −0.5 percent from 2012 to 2017 and −0.6 percent from 2017 to 2023 [[web_3619c407634ed8d7f0a9bbb3]].

INSEE attributes the recent decline to a negative migration balance. From 2015 to 2021, the excess of births over deaths contributed +0.6 percent per year, but the migration deficit reduced the population by 1.2 percent per year, and the natural surplus did not compensate for the migration loss [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]]. The migration deficit applies to all age groups except 18–24-year-olds, reflecting annual arrivals of young workers and students [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]]. INSEE projects that if current trends continue, Paris would have 82,000 fewer residents in 2040 than in 2020, reaching about 2,064,000 [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]].

Paris is also the most densely populated city in France, with about 19,900 inhabitants per km² in 2024 [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]]. INSEE's census data give an average density of 19,959.9 inhabitants per km² for 2023 [[web_01dcf2219a78d49da073bba6]]. Historically, according to Eurostat, the Commune of Paris was the most densely populated city in the European Union in 2012, with 21,616 people per square kilometre within the city limits [[web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162]]. Density is highest in the northern and eastern arrondissements; the 11th arrondissement had a density of 40,672 inhabitants per km² in 1999 [[web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162]].

sections.title: Data sources and reliability
sections.markdown:
The population figures rest on a single authoritative source: INSEE, whose reference populations are census-based, updated annually, and authenticated by decree [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]]. The 2023 reference populations were calculated according to the concepts defined in decree n° 2003-485 of 5 June 2003, as modified, and were authenticated by decree n° 2025-1362 of 26 December 2025 [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]]. INSEE notes that because of the Covid-19 health crisis, the annual census survey scheduled for 2021 was postponed to 2022, and INSEE adapted its calculation methods to continue producing reference populations of quality each year [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]].

Independent aggregators reproduce INSEE figures: citypopulation.de lists 2,103,778 for 2023, citing INSEE as its source [[web_4b9a68f2101be4b45f3c9513]] [[web_955d914bb5822b60e6f8869b]]. The Wikipedia figures, including the 2,047,602 figure for January 2026, are consistent with the INSEE series and the documented decline [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]] [[web_65e4e5164565458316c7430b]]. The Wikipedia Demographics article carries a notice that parts of its statistics sections need updating as of January 2018 [[web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162]], so its older figures should be treated with more caution than the INSEE data; the more recent figures it reports, however, match the INSEE series.

One caveat applies to the density figures: the INSEE English-language dossier for the municipality contains a figure of "1,995,994.3 inhabitants per square kilometre" for 2023 [[web_509ca9307b054327c0afd19e]], which is a transcription error — the French-language dossier gives 19,959.9 for the same year [[web_01dcf2219a78d49da073bba6]], and INSEE's Flash publication gives about 19,900 for 2024 [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]]. The 19,959.9 figure is the correct one and is used here.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.markdown:
The question has a straightforward answer: the capital of France is Paris, and its population is roughly 2.1 million within the city proper. The most authoritative figure is INSEE's legal municipal population of 2,103,778 for the 2023 reference year, in force 1 January 2026 [[web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59]], with more recent estimates showing a slow decline to about 2.05 million by early 2026 [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]] [[web_65e4e5164565458316c7430b]]. The "roughly" in the question is comfortably satisfied by every figure in the evidence pool.

The main qualification a reader should carry away is definitional. "Paris" can mean the commune (about 2.1 million), the Grand Paris cooperation structure (about 6.9 million), the Île-de-France region (about 12.5 million), or the commuter-based metropolitan area (about 15.1 million) [[web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3]] [[web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162]] [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]]. The sources are consistent within each definition, and the differences among the city-proper figures are explained by the documented, ongoing population decline driven by a negative migration balance [[web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a]]. No evidence in the pool contradicts the capital status or the approximate population; the only unresolved point is which boundary the questioner intends, and the answer above gives the city proper as the standard referent while flagging the alternatives.

claim.text: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, located on the Seine in the centre of the Île-de-France region

Its population within the city proper (the commune of Paris) is roughly 2.1 million: the official INSEE legal municipal population for the 2023 reference year is 2,103,778, in force as of 1 January 2026, and recent estimates show a slow decline to about 2.05–2.09 million

Broader definitions are substantially larger: the Paris metropolitan area (aire urbaine) has about 15.1 million inhabitants, the Île-de-France region about 12.5 million, and the Métropole du Grand Paris about 6.9 million
The "roughly 2.1 million" figure refers to the city proper; the wider region is on the order of 12–15 million depending on the definition used
Paris is the capital and largest city of France, with an estimated city population of about 2.04 million in an area of 105.4 km² as of January 2026
It is located on the river Seine in the centre of the Île-de-France region and is the largest metropolitan area in the European Union
Administratively, Paris is both a commune and a department (INSEE code 75056), divided into twenty arrondissements

As the capital, Paris is the seat of France's national government: the President resides at the Élysée Palace, the Prime Minister at the Hôtel Matignon, and both houses of the French Parliament sit on the Rive Gauche — the Senate in the Palais du Luxembourg and the National Assembly in the Palais Bourbon
The city also hosts the headquarters of several international organisations, including UNESCO and the OECD
The capital status is not in dispute across any of the sources; the substantive question is the population figure, which varies by definition and reference date
The authoritative figure for the city proper comes from INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques), France's national statistics institute
For the 2023 reference year, INSEE records a municipal population of 2,103,778 for the commune of Paris, a "counted separately" population of 15,634, and a total population of 2,119,412
These reference populations entered into force on 1 January 2026 and were authenticated by decree n° 2025-1362 of 26 December 2025
The municipal population is the figure used for statistical purposes; the total population is more often used for legislative or regulatory applications
Independent sources reproduce the same 2023 figure
Citypopulation.de, which cites INSEE as its source, lists 2,103,778 for the commune of Paris as of 1 January 2023
INSEE's own dossier complet for the commune confirms 2,103,778 for 2023, alongside 2,187,526 for 2017 and 2,240,621 for 2012
More recent estimates show a continuing decline
INSEE's Flash publication of October 2024 reports 2,087,600 people living in Paris in 2024, 45,500 fewer than three years earlier
The Wikipedia infobox and the EU city list both give 2,047,602 for 1 January 2026, and the European cities list gives 2,048,472 for 1 January 2025

One Wikipedia passage gives 2,102,650 for January 2023, a figure slightly below the INSEE legal population of 2,103,778 for the same reference year — a small discrepancy likely reflecting different estimation methods (annual estimates versus the census-based legal population), but immaterial to the "roughly 2.1 million" answer
The figures are summarised below, drawing on INSEE's legal population, INSEE's Flash estimate, the Wikipedia infobox and EU city list, the European cities list, and citypopulation.de
Source: INSEE legal municipal population; Population: 2,103,778; Reference date: 2023 reference year, in force 1 Jan 2026
Source: INSEE total population (municipal + counted separately); Population: 2,119,412; Reference date: 2023 reference year
Source: INSEE Flash estimate; Population: 2,087,600; Reference date: 2024
Source: Wikipedia infobox / EU city list; Population: 2,047,602; Reference date: 1 Jan 2026
Source: European cities list; Population: 2,048,472; Reference date: 1 Jan 2025
Source: Citypopulation.de; Population: 2,103,778; Reference date: 1 Jan 2023
All of these fall within "roughly 2.1 million" for the city proper

The differences among them reflect the documented ongoing population decline rather than any contradiction among sources: INSEE reports that Paris has been losing residents for decades, with the decline driven by a negative migration balance that the natural surplus does not offset, and the city's population fell by 122,919, about five percent, between 2013 and 2023
The population figure depends heavily on which boundary is used, and the sources are explicit that the city proper is much smaller than the urbanised area around it
The Paris metropolitan area (aire urbaine, as of the 2020 revision) covers 1,929 communes and 18,941 km², with a population of 15,064,617
This statistical area describes the reach of commuter movement to and from Paris and extends beyond the administrative Île-de-France region into nine surrounding departments
Paris itself, at 2,165,423, is the largest city within it
Two other definitions are commonly cited
The Métropole du Grand Paris, an administrative structure for cooperation between Paris and its nearest suburbs created in January 2016, covers 814 km² and had a population of 6.945 million in 2015
The Île-de-France region, the administrative region containing Paris, had a population of 12,463,067 as of January 2023, or 18.3 percent of the population of France
INSEE's Flash publication notes that Paris accounts for 17 percent of the Île-de-France population on less than 1 percent of the regional territory

These are not conflicting figures but different scopes: the city proper (~2.1 million), the Grand Paris cooperation structure (~6.9 million), the region (~12.5 million), and the broader commuter-based metropolitan area (~15.1 million)

A reader asking for "the population of Paris" should be aware that the answer ranges from about 2.1 million to about 15 million depending on the boundary chosen; the city proper is the standard referent for "the capital"
Paris's population has been declining for decades, which explains the small differences among the figures cited above
The city reached a historic high of 2.9 million in 1921, then declined at every census between 1954 and 1999, falling to 2,125,246 in 1999
INSEE's official series shows 2,590,771 in 1968 falling to 2,103,778 in 2023, with a mid-2000s rebound to 2,240,621 in 2012
The decline resumed after 2012: the average annual change was −0.5 percent from 2012 to 2017 and −0.6 percent from 2017 to 2023
INSEE attributes the recent decline to a negative migration balance
